description: The objective of the Rodent Research-9 (RR-9) mission was to use mice to understand the molecular basis of phenomena that affect astronauts during long-duration spaceflight, particularly visual impairment and joint tissue degradation. To this end, a flight group (FLT) of 10 week-old male C57BL/6J mice were launched from Kennedy Space Center (KSC) on 8/14/2017 and housed in Rodent Habitats on the ISS for 33 days before being returned alive to Earth. After splashdown in the Pacific Ocean, the animals were transported to Loma Linda University (LLU) for testing, euthanasia and dissection on 9/18/2018. A Basal Control (BSL) was housed in standard cages at Kennedy Space Center (KSC) and euthanized one day after launch of the FLT animals (8/15/2017). Ground Control (GC) and Vivarium Control (VIV) studies were planned to commence at KSC approximately one-week after the conclusion of the flight experiments. However, all the GC and VIV mouse studies at KSC had to be cancelled due to Hurricane Irma and potential adverse effects on the animal housing facility. The GC and VIV studies were therefore rescheduled and begun in May, 2018. The GC was euthanized and dissected 6/18/2018 - 6/20/2018, while the VIV was euthanized and dissected 6/22/2018 - 6/23/2018. Because this resulted in a different cohort of mice being used for the GC and VIV controls as compared to the flight (FLT) and basal (BSL) groups, two cohort controls were included in the study. The first, Cohort Control 1 (CC_C1), was from the same cohort as the FLT and BSL animals, and was sacrificed and dissected 4 days after the FLT group (9/22/2017). The second, Cohort Control 2 (CC_C2), was from the same cohort as the GC and VIV animals, and was sacrificed and dissected 2-8 days after the GC and VIV groups, (6/24/2018 - 6/26/2018). The CC_C1 and CC_C2 groups were housed in standard cages and fed standard chow in contrast to all other groups which received Rodent Foodbars. To clarify the connections between treatment groups and animal cohorts, the following group abbreviations are used in the sample metadata: Flight (FLT_C1); Basal (BSL_C1); Ground Control (GC_C2); Vivarium Control (VIV_C2), Cohort Control 1 (CC_C1); Cohort Control 2 (CC_C2). Upon dissection, livers were preserved in liquid nitrogen and stored at -80 C before RNA was extracted, libraries generated (stranded, ribodepleted) and sequenced (target 60 M clusters at PE 150 bp).
funding: The sequencing analysis was funded by NASA Space Biology Program Office, Space Life and Physical Sciences Research and Applications Division through a collaborative effort with GeneLab.

payloads.description:
The Rodent Research 9 (RR-9) payload consisted of three space biology experiments that examined the impacts of long-duration spaceflight on human tissue and systems, aiming to better understand the visual impairment and joint tissue degradation that affected astronauts and to investigate possible ways to counteract those health problems. One investigation studied the effects of microgravity on fluid shifts and increased fluid pressures that occurred in the head. A second examined the impact of spaceflight on the vessels that supplied blood to the eyes. The third investigated the extent of knee and hip joint degradation caused by prolonged exposure to weightlessness.

NASA's Space Life and Physical Sciences (SLPS) partnered with Russia's Institute of Biomedical Problems (IMBP) to establish a collaborative and multidisciplinary study to examine the effects of spaceflight on various physiological systems. This mission was sponsored by the NASA Space Biology Program.

The objectives of the Investigator team’s studies were to evaluate physiological changes in mice that occurred during a long-duration spaceflight mission in low Earth orbit. Maximal science return was achieved by distributing dissected tissues from the animals to as many Russian and NASA investigators as possible via the SLPS Biospecimen Sharing Program (BSP) and through agreements with the IMBP.

Twenty (20) mice (male, C57BL/6) between 8–16 weeks old were launched in one Transporter (10 mice per side), transferred to Rodent Habitats onboard the International Space Station (ISS), and maintained in microgravity for approximately 30 days (the SpaceX Dragon docked period). Nominally, no crew activities were required except for standard animal transfers between the Transporter and Habitats, and other activities required to ensure animal welfare, such as health checks and NuRFB replenishments.
Prior to Dragon unberth, all twenty mice were transferred into a clean Transporter, followed by transfer to a Dragon capsule and then returned to Earth alive (live animal return [LAR]). The duration from splashdown to handover of the mice payload was approximately 48–72 hours. After the handover of the mice to the NASA Rodent Research team, the mice were immediately transported to a facility approved for conducting post-flight rodent gait assessment and dissections. This facility was located as close to the payload handover location as possible to minimize the total duration the mice were exposed to 1G post-splashdown. The primary investigator teams, BSP teams, and the Rodent Research dissection Lead and team conducted the dissection process at this facility immediately following a health check, specimen sampling, and acquisition of walking kinematic data.

The Rodent Research 9 (RR-9) science investigation was conducted by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration’s Space Life and Physical Sciences program. The mission consisted of three experiments led by principal investigators Michael Delp, Xiao Wen Mao, and Jeffrey Willey. Delp’s investigation studied the effects of long-duration spaceflight on fluid shifts and increased fluid pressures in the head, Mao’s examined the impact of spaceflight on the vessels that supplied blood to the eyes, and Willey’s investigated the extent of knee and hip joint degradation caused by prolonged exposure to weightlessness. Specific aims of each experiment are summarized below.

The mission objectives

Michael Delp’s experiment had four aims:
-	To determine whether spaceflight on the ISS altered rodent basilar artery spontaneous tone, myogenic and KCl (Potassium Chloride)-evoked vasoconstriction, mechanical stiffness, and gross structure.
-	To estimate whether spaceflight on the ISS altered the blood-brain barrier in rodents, as indicated by ultrastructural examination of the junctional complex of the cerebral capillary endothelium.
-	To determine whether spaceflight on the ISS altered rodent basal vein (inside cranium) and jugular vein (outside cranium) spontaneous tone, myogenic and KCl-evoked constriction, distension, and gross structure.
-	To determine whether spaceflight on the ISS altered the ability of the cervical lymphatics to modulate lymph flow, and thus, regulate cerebral fluid homeostasis.

Xiao Wen Mao’s investigation had two aims:
-	To define the relationships between spaceflight condition-induced oxidative stress in reactive oxygen species (ROS) expression and retinal vascular remodeling and BRB function in mice that returned to Earth alive.
-	To determine whether spaceflight condition-induced oxidative damage in the retina was mediated through photoreceptor mitochondrial ROS production.

Jeffrey Willey’s investigation had two aims:
-	To determine the extent of knee and hip joint degradation in mice after 30 days of spaceflight on the ISS.
-	To use the DigiGait System to assess gait patterns before and after returning from the ISS.

IACUC Protocol Number: FLT-17-107

All animal procedures performed in these experiments were approved by the Institutional Animal Care and Use Committees (IACUC), with protocol numbers NASA: FLT-17-107 for flight at the NASA Ames Research Center (ARC) and the Kennedy Space Center (KSC), and the methods were carried out in accordance with relevant guidelines and regulations.

NASA Space Biology Biospecimen Sharing Program Activities
N/A


Available Data
The RR payload produced the following Data (from checklist Excel file):
-	Animal enclosure temperature and relative humidity flight and ground data
-	Live Animal Return sensor accelerometer data
-	ISS cabin and ground simulation chamber environmental monitoring data
-	Rodent data including preflight data, operations time logs, sample shipment data
-	Flight and ground animal behavior video, available for request

protocols.description: A cohort of 10 week-old male C57BL/6J mice (Jackson Laboratory) were launched in one Transporter (10 mice per side), transferred to Rodent Habitats onboard the International Space Station (ISS) and maintained in microgravity for ~33 days (the SpaceX Dragon docked period). No crew activities were required except for standard animal transfers between the Transporter and Habitats, and other activities required to ensure animal welfare, such as health checks and NuRFB replenishments.    Prior to Dragon unberth, all mice were transferred into a clean Transporter followed by transfer to a Dragon capsule and then returned to Earth alive. The duration from splashdown to handover of the mice payload at the pier was approximately 24 hours. After handover of mice to the NASA Rodent Research team, the mice were immediately transported to the animal facility at Loma Linda University for conducting post-flight rodent gait assessment and dissections. The primary investigator teams, BSP teams, and Rodent Research dissection Lead and team conducted the dissection process at LLU immediately following a health check and specimen sampling and acquisition of walking kinematic data and intraocular pressure (IOP) measurements.  A Basal Control (BSL) was housed in standard cages at Kennedy Space Center (KSC) and euthanized one day after launch of the FLT animals. Ground Control (GC) and Vivarium Control (VIV) studies were planned to commence at KSC approximately one-week after the conclusion of the flight experiments.  Early termination of RR-9 Ground Control (GC): Due to Hurricane Irma in September 2017 in Florida, the RR9 GC experiments were prematurely terminated. The experiment was repeated in May 2018 using the same strain of mice that was used for the flight experiment to match with flight animals. Besides Ground Control and Vivarium groups, an additional group of animals was used as Cohort Controls (Cohort Control #2) to normalize the variation due to differences in the cohorts.  Cohort control #1 and #2 animals (CC) were not provided with the rodent food bars, lixits, or raised wire floors.
protocols.name: animal husbandry

protocols.description: Mice were euthanized, upon live animal return and dissected immediately. Each carcass dissection time was no longer than 1 hour from collection of the first tissue. Multiple tissues, including the liver tissue, were collected from each carcass.
protocols.name: sample collection

protocols.description: RNA was extracted using the AllPrep DNA/RNA Mini Kit (Qiagen, Valencia, CA). Homogenization buffer for RNA purification was made by adding 1:100 beta-mercaptoethanol to Buffer RLT (Qiagen, Valencia, CA) and kept on ice until use. After thawing on ice, approximately 30 mg of tissue was isolated using a scalpel, weighed and immediately placed in 600 uL of the Buffer RLT solution. Each sample was then homogenized for approximately 20 seconds at 20,000 RPM using a Polytron PT1300D handheld homogenizer with a 5 mm standard dispersing aggregate tip (Kinematica, Bohemia, NY). Homogenates were centrifuged for 3 minutes at RT and at 14,000 X g to remove cell debris. The supernatant from each sample was then used to isolate and purify RNA following the manufacturer protocol. RNA was eluted in 50 uL H2O. Concentration for all RNA samples were measured using Qubit 3.0 Fluorometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA). RNA quality was assessed using the Agilent 2100 Bioanalyzer with the Agilent RNA 6000 Nano Kit or Agilent RNA 6000 Pico Kit (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA).
protocols.name: nucleic acid extraction

protocols.description: ERCC ExFold RNA Spike-In Mixes (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Waltham, MA Cat # 4456739, v92) at 1:100 dilution of either Mix 1 or Mix 2 were added immediately after RNA extractions at the concentrations suggested by the manufacturer protocol.
protocols.name: spike-in protocol

protocols.description: RNA ribo depletion was done with Illumina TruSeq Stranded Total RNA Library Prep Gold. Input RNA were approximately 500 ng with RIN greater than 4. Index adapters were 1.5 uM (IDT, 384-well xGen Dual Index UMI Adapters). 15 cycles PCR were performed. Library fragment size ~300 bp was assessed using Agilent 4200 TapeStation with D1000 DNA ScreenTape (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA). Pooled library concentration was measured by Universal qPCR Master Mix (Kapa Biosystems, Wilmington, MA). Library quality control was determined by iSeq100 (Illumina, San Diego, CA).
protocols.name: library construction

protocols.description: RNA sequencing was performed by GeneLab Sample Processing Lab on Illumina NovaSeq 6000. Paired end 149bp. PhiX included as control.
protocols.name: nucleic acid sequencing

protocols.description: Quality assessment of reads was performed with FastQC v0.12.1 and reports were combined with MultiQC v1.26. rRNA percentages of reads were estimated with the 'hts_SeqScreener' program of htstream v1.0.0.
protocols.name: GeneLab raw data processing protocol

protocols.description: Data were processed as described in GL-DPPD-7101-G (https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab_Data_Processing/blob/master/RNAseq/Pipeline_GL-DPPD-7101_Versions/GL-DPPD-7101-G.md), using NF_RCP version 2.1.0 (https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab_RNASeq_Workflow/tree/NF_RCP_2.1.0). In short, raw fastq files were filtered using Trim Galore! (version 0.6.10) powered by Cutadapt (version 4.2). Trimmed fastq file quality was evaluated with FastQC (version 0.12.1), and MultiQC (version 1.26) was used to generate MultiQC reports. Mus Musculus STAR and RSEM references were built using STAR (version 2.7.11b) and RSEM (version 1.3.3), respectively, Ensembl release 112, genome assembly GRCm39 (Mus_musculus.GRCm39.dna.primary_assembly.fa) concatenated with ERCC92.fa from ThermoFisher (https://assets.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/ERCC92.zip), and the following gtf annotation file: Mus_musculus.GRCm39.112.gtf concatenated with the ERCC92.gtf file from ThermoFisher (https://assets.thermofisher.com/TFS-Assets/LSG/manuals/ERCC92.zip). Trimmed reads were aligned to the Mus Musculus + ERCC STAR reference with STAR (version 2.7.11b) and alignment log files were compiled with MultiQC (version 1.26). Aligned reads were assessed for strandedness using RSeQC infer_experiment.py (version 5.0.4), gene body coverage using RSeQC geneBody_coverage.py (version 5.0.4), inner distance was assessed using RSeQC inner_distance.py (version 5.0.4), and distribution of RNA features using RSeQC read_distribution.py (version 5.0.4). Aligned reads from all samples were quantified using RSEM (version 1.3.3), with strandedness set to forward and RSEM count log files were compiled with MultiQC (version 1.26). To create a set of rRNA-removed quantification data, Ensembl IDs mapping to ribosomal RNA (rRNA) were removed from the RSEM gene count data. Both the original set of RSEM quantification data and the rRNA-removed data were subject to differential gene expression analysis as follows. A runsheet was generated with dp_tools (version 1.3.8) and the runsheet and quantification data were imported to R (version 4.4.2) with tximport (version 1.34.0), ERCC genes were removed, and the non-ERCC genes were normalized with DESeq2 (version 1.46.0) median of ratios method. Normalized gene counts were subject to differential expression analysis. Differential expression analysis was performed in R (version 4.4.2) using DESeq2 (version 1.46.0); all groups were compared pairwise using the Wald test and the likelihood ratio test was used to generate the F statistic p-value. Gene annotations were assigned using the custom annotation tables generated in-house as detailed in GL-DPPD-7110-A (https://github.com/nasa/GeneLab_Data_Processing/blob/GL_RefAnnotTable-A_1.1.0/GeneLab_Reference_Annotations/Pipeline_GL-DPPD-7110_Versions/GL-DPPD-7110-A/GL-DPPD-7110-A.md), with STRINGdb (version 2.16.4), PANTHER.db (version 1.0.12), and org.Mm.eg.db (version 3.19.1). Assessment of ERCC spiked genes was performed as detailed in the ERCC_analysis_GLbulkRNAseq.html report.
protocols.name: GeneLab RNAseq data processing protocol
